description: One specialist's reading list: a computational neuroscientist whose shelf is dominated by ten tightly related neuroscience sub-areas, with a small tail of Buddhism and carpentry. It tests whether topic clustering can split a large single-field shelf finely while still isolating the tiny unrelated areas.
profile: Computational neuroscientist. Also reads a little about Buddhism and does carpentry at weekends.

articles.title: Border Ownership and Figure-Ground Signals in V2
articles.gist: Describes neurons that signal which side of an edge belongs to the object, and discusses whether feedback from higher areas supplies that information.

articles.title: Pupil-Linked Arousal and Learning Rate Adaptation
articles.gist: Pupil dilation tracks surprise in changing environments and predicts how strongly people update beliefs, suggesting noradrenergic regulation of the learning rate.

articles.title: Metacognitive Confidence as Second-Order Prediction
articles.gist: Proposes that confidence reports track the estimated precision of one's own perceptual inference and reviews human fMRI and behavioural evidence from prefrontal regions.

articles.title: Successor Representations and the Hippocampus-Striatum Dialogue
articles.gist: Argues that predictive maps of future state occupancy bridge model-free and model-based control, and reviews behavioural dissociations in humans that support the idea.

articles.title: Local Sleep in Awake Cortex: Neuronal Off Periods After Prolonged Wakefulness
articles.gist: Shows that patches of cortex briefly go silent in rats kept awake, linking local sleep to errors in performance.

articles.title: Pattern Separation in the Dentate Gyrus: Sparse Codes and Adult Neurogenesis
articles.gist: Examines how dentate granule cells decorrelate similar inputs and what newly born neurons add, including modelling and behavioural discrimination tasks.

articles.title: Expectation Suppression Without Attention: A Repetition Study in Macaque IT
articles.gist: Shows that responses in inferotemporal cortex shrink for expected image pairs even when attention is held constant, dissociating prediction effects from simple adaptation.

articles.title: Brain-Computer Interfaces for Paralysis: Ten Years of Intracortical Decoding
articles.gist: Surveys intracortical decoders that let people with paralysis control cursors and robot arms, and asks what learning on the part of the user contributes.

articles.title: Human Single-Neuron Recordings of Concept Cells
articles.gist: Describes neurons in the human medial temporal lobe responding to specific people or places across photographs and names, and what that suggests about episodic encoding.

articles.title: Population Codes for Natural Movies in Mouse V1
articles.gist: Analyses large-scale recordings during natural movie viewing and shows how stimulus information is spread across a distributed population with substantial shared variability.

articles.title: Resting-State Networks: Real Organisation or Artifact of Motion?
articles.gist: Reviews the debate over head motion and physiological noise in functional connectivity, and the preprocessing strategies that reduce spurious correlations.

articles.title: Cognitive Control, Conflict and the Anterior Cingulate Cortex
articles.gist: Evaluates conflict monitoring accounts of the anterior cingulate and alternatives based on expected value of control, with recordings and imaging.

articles.title: Memory for Reward Context: Dopamine Modulation of Hippocampal Encoding
articles.gist: Examines how dopamine from the ventral tegmental area enhances hippocampal memory for surprising or rewarding events and the controversy over its source.

articles.title: Why Do Cortical Responses Get Sparser as Stimuli Become Familiar?
articles.gist: Examines familiarity-driven sparsening of population responses, comparing explanations from efficient coding, error minimisation and inhibitory plasticity in recordings from rodent sensory cortex.

articles.title: Sensorimotor Noise and Why Practice Reduces Variability
articles.gist: Argues that skill acquisition reshapes the structure of motor variability, shifting it into dimensions that do not hurt task performance.

articles.title: Dopamine-Gated Plasticity at Corticostriatal Synapses
articles.gist: Describes how dopamine receptor subtypes on direct and indirect pathway neurons convert coincident spiking into long-term potentiation or depression, and why the timing window matters.

articles.title: Credit Assignment Without Backprop: Dopamine and Eligibility Traces
articles.gist: Examines synaptic eligibility traces that let a delayed dopamine signal strengthen the right inputs, with evidence from striatal slice recordings.

articles.title: Neural Trajectories During Reaching Are Conserved Across Animals
articles.gist: Aligns population activity from different monkeys and shows that the underlying dynamics are shared, enabling decoders to transfer across individuals.

articles.title: Decoding Mental Content With Multivoxel Pattern Analysis: Possibilities and Pitfalls
articles.gist: Explains classifiers, searchlights and cross-validation errors, with examples of circular analyses that inflated apparent decoding performance.

articles.title: Neuropixels and the New Scale of Systems Neuroscience
articles.gist: A long-form piece on how recording thousands of neurons at once is changing experiments, data handling and what questions are even worth asking.

articles.title: The Forward Model Doing Its Job: Corollary Discharge in Saccades
articles.gist: Shows how the brain compensates for self-generated eye movement and what disruption of the corollary discharge pathway does to visual stability.

articles.title: Computational Psychiatry of Anhedonia: Reduced Reward Sensitivity or Learning Rates?
articles.gist: Fits reinforcement learning models to depressed patients and finds blunted sensitivity rather than slower learning, with implications for how behavioural tasks are interpreted.

articles.title: Nagarjuna's Emptiness Without Mysticism
articles.gist: A readable introduction to the Madhyamaka argument that nothing has intrinsic existence, with discussion of how the idea has been misread as nihilism.

articles.title: Grid Cells and the Geometry of Thought
articles.gist: Surveys evidence that entorhinal grid codes extend beyond space to abstract conceptual dimensions, and asks what the hexagonal pattern buys for generalisation.

articles.title: Dendrites as Prediction Machines: Apical Inputs and Context
articles.gist: Reviews the idea that apical dendrites of layer 5 pyramidal cells carry contextual predictions that gate somatic output, with evidence from calcium spikes during behaviour.

articles.title: Recollection Versus Familiarity: Two Processes or One Strength?
articles.gist: A review of the dual-process debate, evaluating receiver operating characteristic analyses, lesion patterns and imaging dissociations across perirhinal and hippocampal regions.

articles.title: Synaptic Changes in Motor Cortex During Skill Learning
articles.gist: Imaging of dendritic spines in mouse motor cortex reveals rapid formation of new spines during a lever-press task that persist in the long term.

articles.title: The Bayesian Brain Is Not a Calculator: Approximate Inference in Neural Circuits
articles.gist: Argues that real circuits approximate posterior inference with sampling or variational shortcuts, and surveys what each scheme predicts about variability, noise correlations and response timing.

articles.title: Local Learning Rules That Approximate Backprop in Cortex
articles.gist: Reviews biologically plausible schemes in which prediction errors propagate through dendritic compartments, allowing deep networks to learn without symmetric weight transport.

articles.title: Magnetoencephalography and the Timing of Cognition
articles.gist: Introduces MEG source reconstruction for tracking fast neural events, comparing its spatial limits with EEG and fMRI.

articles.title: Foraging Decisions and the Marginal Value Theorem in the Brain
articles.gist: Humans and monkeys decide when to leave a depleting patch, and anterior cingulate activity tracks the average reward rate that the theorem says should guide leaving.

articles.title: What Does the BOLD Signal Really Measure?
articles.gist: A primer on neurovascular coupling, covering oxygenation, blood volume and flow, and the conditions under which BOLD diverges from neural spiking.

articles.title: Cerebellar Learning and Climbing Fibre Error Signals
articles.gist: Examines how Purkinje cells use climbing fibre inputs as teaching signals to recalibrate movements, with evidence from eyeblink conditioning and saccade adaptation.

articles.title: Interoception and the Predictive Self
articles.gist: A long-form essay on how inferences about bodily states may ground emotion and self-experience, drawing on heartbeat-evoked potentials and insular cortex recordings.

articles.title: Metaplasticity and the BCM Rule: A Sliding Threshold
articles.gist: Revisits the idea that the threshold for potentiation shifts with prior activity, covering experimental tests and relevance for stability of learning.

articles.title: A Thalamic Pacemaker for Sleep Spindles
articles.gist: Traces spindle generation to interactions between thalamic reticular nucleus and thalamocortical relay cells, with modelling and pharmacological manipulations.

articles.title: Active Inference in Practice: What a Generative Model Buys You
articles.gist: A tutorial-style post building a toy agent that picks actions by minimising expected free energy, with candid notes on where the maths hides engineering choices.

articles.title: A Mathematical Reading of Rao and Ballard's 1999 Model
articles.gist: Walks through the original hierarchical predictive coding network line by line, noting which assumptions have survived two decades of physiology and which have quietly been dropped.

articles.title: Long-Term Potentiation Is Not Memory: Notes on a Slippery Equivalence
articles.gist: An essay asking when it is legitimate to treat synaptic strengthening in a slice as a model for memory in behaving animals, and what evidence would settle it.

articles.title: Local Error Signals Drive Dendritic Plasticity
articles.gist: Shows that plasticity at apical synapses depends on top-down mismatch signals and links the biophysics to credit assignment in deep cortical hierarchies.

articles.title: Cortical Magnification and the Cost of Foveal Vision
articles.gist: Argues that overrepresentation of the fovea in cortex shapes crowding and acuity, with fMRI measurements across the visual field.

articles.title: Spinal Central Pattern Generators and the Locomotor Rhythm
articles.gist: Describes how interneuron circuits in the spinal cord produce alternating limb movements, and how descending commands modulate speed and gait.

articles.title: Pattern Completion as Inference: A Generative View of Recall
articles.gist: Frames memory retrieval as inference in a learned generative model, linking hippocampal completion with cortical priors and explaining systematic gist-based distortions in recall.

articles.title: Natural Image Statistics and the Design of Early Vision
articles.gist: Shows that sparse coding of natural scenes yields Gabor-like filters, and examines how well later predictions about higher-order statistics hold up.

articles.title: Time Cells in CA1 and the Representation of Elapsed Intervals
articles.gist: Records sequences of neurons that fire at successive moments during delays, and tests whether they encode time itself or the progression of ongoing events.

articles.title: Attentional Modulation of Visual Responses: Gain, Normalisation and Noise
articles.gist: Compares how attention changes firing rates and correlated variability across the visual hierarchy, and what readout of those changes explains behavioural improvement.

articles.title: The Hippocampus as a Predictive Map
articles.gist: Develops the successor representation as an account of place cell firing and shows it explains the influence of behaviour on field shape.

articles.title: Attention as Precision Optimisation: Testing the Equivalence
articles.gist: Tests whether spatial attention behaves like a change in the precision assigned to prediction errors, using orientation discrimination and gain measures in early visual cortex.

articles.title: Mind Wandering and the Default Mode Network
articles.gist: Shows how activity in default mode regions rises as attention drifts from a task, and argues for a more nuanced view of what mind wandering does.

articles.title: Efference Copy and the Cerebellum: A Forward-Model Primer
articles.gist: Explains how motor commands generate predicted sensory consequences, why tickling yourself fails, and what cerebellar lesions reveal about the forward model's neural basis.

articles.title: How the Brain Tracks Tool Use: Body Schema in Parietal Cortex
articles.gist: Reviews neurons that treat a held tool as an extension of the arm and the broader question of how body representation updates during action.

articles.title: The Reliability of fMRI: Test-Retest Problems in Individual Differences
articles.gist: Shows that many task activation measures have poor test-retest reliability, which undermines brain-behaviour correlations, and proposes ways to measure reliability.

articles.title: Functional Ultrasound Imaging: A New Window on the Awake Brain
articles.gist: Describes a method that tracks cerebral blood volume at high resolution through the skull of moving animals, and the questions it makes tractable.

articles.title: Colour in the Cortex: Double-Opponent Cells and Beyond
articles.gist: Reviews the cell types that carry hue information from retina to cortex and the unresolved question of where unique hues are represented.

articles.title: Why Do We Sleep? The Synaptic Homeostasis Hypothesis Under Scrutiny
articles.gist: Evaluates the proposal that sleep downscales synapses that wakefulness strengthened, with ultrastructural data, proteomics and critiques about alternative functions.

articles.title: Pulvinar Contributions to Attention and Cortical Communication
articles.gist: Examines the thalamic pulvinar as a regulator of information flow between visual areas and tests the effect of inactivation on attention-related synchrony.

articles.title: Optimal Feedback Control as a Theory of Reaching
articles.gist: Introduces a framework in which the brain minimises a cost under noise and corrects only errors that matter, accounting for variability patterns in human arm movements.

articles.title: Frontal Eye Fields and the Priority Map
articles.gist: Reviews a spatial priority map integrating bottom-up salience and top-down goals, and the evidence from microstimulation that frontal activity directs covert attention.

articles.title: Is Dopamine a Reward Prediction Error or a Movement Signal?
articles.gist: Reviews the debate over whether striatal dopamine release tracks prediction error, motivation or vigor, using fibre photometry during self-paced locomotion and cued tasks.

articles.title: Homeostatic Scaling: How Neurons Keep Their Firing Rate in Check
articles.gist: Describes multiplicative scaling of synaptic strength after activity blockade and the signalling pathways that implement it, with in vivo evidence from visual cortex.

articles.title: Retinotopy Beyond V1: Mapping Human Visual Field Maps With Population Receptive Fields
articles.gist: Describes methods for estimating receptive field size and position across visual areas and what the results say about hierarchy and eccentricity bias.

articles.title: Motion Integration in Area MT: Pattern and Component Cells
articles.gist: Investigates how neurons in the middle temporal area combine local motion signals into the perceived direction of a moving object, with microstimulation causality tests.

articles.title: Noise Correlations and the Limits of Population Coding
articles.gist: Reviews how shared variability among neurons restricts information in large populations, and which kinds of correlations help or hurt a downstream decoder.

articles.title: Learning the Statistics of Natural Sounds in Auditory Cortex
articles.gist: Shows that neurons in auditory cortex tune to temporal regularities of ecological sounds and update quickly as the acoustic environment changes across recording sessions.

articles.title: Cross-Modal Attention: Sounds That Sharpen Sight
articles.gist: Shows that a sound at a location transiently enhances visual processing there, with ERP and fMRI evidence for early modulation in sensory cortex.

articles.title: Locus Coeruleus and Adaptive Gain: Noradrenaline in Focus
articles.gist: Argues that noradrenergic neurons tune the balance between exploitation and exploration, and shows how pupil diameter tracks their activity.

articles.title: Sleep-Dependent Synaptic Remodelling in Mouse Cortex
articles.gist: Imaging reveals that spine formation after learning needs subsequent sleep, and suggests slow oscillations facilitate selective strengthening of recently active connections.

articles.title: Hierarchical Gaussian Filtering for Learning Under Volatility
articles.gist: Introduces a hierarchical model where beliefs about environmental volatility set the learning rate, then applies it to behaviour and pupil data in changing reward environments.

articles.title: Reading Out Memories From Hippocampal fMRI With Representational Similarity
articles.gist: Applies pattern similarity analyses to high-resolution imaging of hippocampal subfields to test whether remembered episodes leave distinguishable multivoxel traces.

articles.title: Predictive Processing and the Psychosis Continuum
articles.gist: Reviews proposals that aberrant precision weighting of priors versus sensory evidence explains hallucinations and delusions, and weighs the supporting behavioural evidence against failed replications.

articles.title: Dendritic Computation: NMDA Spikes and Nonlinear Integration
articles.gist: Argues that local dendritic nonlinearities make single neurons far more powerful than point units, and what that means for learning rules.

articles.title: Catastrophic Forgetting and How Synapses Avoid It
articles.gist: Compares synaptic consolidation models that make important weights harder to change with continual learning methods in machine learning.

articles.title: Blindsight and the Unconscious Pathways of Vision
articles.gist: Reviews patients with V1 damage who respond to stimuli they cannot see and what the residual pathways through the superior colliculus tell us.

articles.title: Neural Manifolds: What Does Dimensionality Reduction Actually Show?
articles.gist: A critical essay cautioning that low dimensionality can reflect stimulus smoothness or analysis choices rather than circuit constraints, and proposing controls.

articles.title: Attention as Learned Action: Reinforcement Learning of Where to Look
articles.gist: Argues that attentional deployment can be trained by reward, reviewing value-driven attentional capture and neural correlates in visual cortex and the superior colliculus.

articles.title: Representational Drift: Stable Behaviour, Changing Neurons
articles.gist: Surveys findings that tuning of individual neurons changes across days even though behaviour does not, and the computational proposals for maintaining a stable readout.

articles.title: Habit Formation and Dorsolateral Striatum: A Reappraisal
articles.gist: Questions the clean split between goal-directed and habitual control, reviewing lesion and recording studies suggesting the dorsolateral striatum encodes action chunks more than stimulus-response links.

articles.title: Contour Integration and Association Fields
articles.gist: Shows how long-range horizontal connections in V1 link collinear edges, and links the anatomy to psychophysical findings about detecting curves in clutter.

articles.title: Motor Adaptation: Fast and Slow States of Learning
articles.gist: Models learning of force-field perturbations as two parallel processes with different time constants and explains savings and spontaneous recovery.

articles.title: Excitatory-Inhibitory Balance and Chaotic Cortical Activity
articles.gist: Describes balanced networks that produce irregular firing without tuning, and what such models predict about response to perturbation.

articles.title: Boundary Cells, Object Vector Cells and the Building Blocks of Cognitive Maps
articles.gist: Catalogues the zoo of spatially tuned cells beyond place and grid cells and discusses how they might be combined into flexible maps.

articles.title: Attention and Encoding: Why Distracted Learning Leaves Weak Memories
articles.gist: Reviews how divided attention at study impairs hippocampal encoding and tests the claim that attentional lapses reduce subsequent memory through theta power.

articles.title: Negative Prediction Errors and the Lateral Habenula
articles.gist: Reviews how the lateral habenula signals disappointment and punishment through rostromedial tegmental nucleus, inhibiting dopamine cells and shaping avoidance learning.

articles.title: Dreaming as Generative Replay: A Neural Network Perspective
articles.gist: An essay asking whether dreams function like synthetic data for training, with parallels to wake-sleep algorithms and overfitting-prevention hypotheses.

articles.title: Low-Rank Recurrent Networks and the Dimensionality of Neural Computation
articles.gist: Links the rank of connectivity in trained recurrent networks to the dimensionality of their activity, offering a framework for interpreting population recordings.

articles.title: Canonical Microcircuits for Predictive Coding in Laminar Cortex
articles.gist: Maps prediction and prediction-error units onto the layers of a cortical column, and reviews laminar recordings that partly support the proposed assignment of superficial and deep pyramidal cells.

articles.title: Motor Learning With Reward Only: Reinforcement Without Error Feedback
articles.gist: Participants learn reaching movements guided solely by binary success signals, and the paper asks how reward-driven learning differs from error-based adaptation.

articles.title: Surround Suppression Varies With Contrast: A Normalisation Account
articles.gist: Fits divisive normalisation models to responses in cat and macaque V1 and shows that a single canonical computation can explain many context effects.

articles.title: CaMKII and the Molecular Basis of Long-Term Memory
articles.gist: Traces the autophosphorylation story of CaMKII as a memory switch, and discusses its persistence, turnover and the doubts raised by recent knockdown studies.

articles.title: Perception as Controlled Hallucination: Notes From a Skeptic
articles.gist: A blog post questioning the popular slogan, separating the sound core of generative models from the loose metaphors that have grown around it in popular science.

articles.title: Motor Cortex Is Not a Muscle Map: The Dynamical Systems Turn
articles.gist: Argues that motor cortex generates movement through rotational population dynamics rather than encoding muscle activity directly, reviewing the rise of that view and its remaining puzzles.

articles.title: Mixed Selectivity in Prefrontal Neurons Enables Flexible Cognition
articles.gist: Argues that neurons responding to nonlinear mixtures of task variables give the population high-dimensional representations that linear readouts can exploit.

articles.title: Model-Based Planning in Rodents: What the Two-Step Task Can and Cannot Tell Us
articles.gist: A critique of the two-step task, showing that apparent model-based behaviour can arise from simpler strategies, with simulations of the confounds and suggested redesigns.

articles.title: Behavioural Timescale Plasticity Creates Place Fields in a Single Trial
articles.gist: Shows that a plateau potential in CA1 dendrites can establish a place field in one lap, with a plasticity rule extending across seconds.

articles.title: Notes From a Ten-Day Vipassana Retreat
articles.gist: A first-person account of silent meditation, covering the boredom, the physical pain, shifts in attention and what the author took home afterwards.

articles.title: Vigor, Dopamine and the Cost of Moving Fast
articles.gist: A model in which tonic dopamine reports average reward rate, setting the opportunity cost of time and therefore how vigorously animals perform actions.

articles.title: Memory Indexing Theory After Forty Years
articles.gist: A retrospective on the proposal that hippocampus stores pointers to cortical patterns rather than content, and how modern recordings have refined or challenged it.

articles.title: The Four Noble Truths as a Medical Framework
articles.gist: Argues that the Buddha's teaching has the structure of a diagnosis, aetiology, prognosis and treatment, and considers what that says about the aims of practice.

articles.title: Inattentional Blindness: How Much Do We Really Miss?
articles.gist: A long-form piece on classic invisible gorilla experiments, with neuroscience of why unattended stimuli are poorly encoded and what that means for everyday perception.

articles.title: Structural Plasticity: Dendritic Spine Turnover in Learning
articles.gist: Longitudinal two-photon imaging shows that spines appear and vanish during learning, with a subset stabilising over months.

articles.title: Visual Recognition Memory in the Perirhinal Cortex
articles.gist: Shows that neurons in the perirhinal cortex respond differently to novel and familiar images, linking ventral stream representation to memory judgements.

articles.title: Synaptic Tagging and Capture: Making Early Plasticity Last
articles.gist: Explains how a weakly stimulated synapse can acquire late-phase potentiation if a nearby synapse triggers protein synthesis, and considers behavioural analogues.

articles.title: Attention Shapes Population Noise: Shared Variability in Area V4
articles.gist: Finds that attention reduces noise correlations among neurons and argues the resulting boost in population information exceeds gains from firing rate changes alone.

articles.title: Mindfulness Meditation Without the Metaphysics: A Secular Critique
articles.gist: Examines how clinical mindfulness programmes were abstracted from Buddhist context, and asks what is gained and lost when ethics and doctrine are removed.

articles.title: The Calcium Control Hypothesis of Synaptic Plasticity
articles.gist: Explains how the amplitude and duration of postsynaptic calcium decide between potentiation and depression, with models fit to slice experiments.

articles.title: Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity: Beyond the Pairing Protocol
articles.gist: Reviews how STDP behaves with natural spike trains, finding the simple pair-based rule inadequate and proposing triplet and calcium-based alternatives.

articles.title: Inhibitory Plasticity and Excitation-Inhibition Balance
articles.gist: Shows how plasticity at inhibitory synapses can restore balance after learning and explains how it may protect memories from overwriting.

articles.title: REM Sleep and Emotional Memory Processing
articles.gist: Reviews evidence that REM, with low noradrenaline, depotentiates the emotional charge of memories, and presents mixed findings from human sleep deprivation studies.

articles.title: Whatever Happened to the Free-Energy Principle? A Skeptical Ten-Year Audit
articles.gist: A critical review asking what the free-energy principle has actually predicted, which claims were falsifiable, and why many experimentalists treat it as a framework rather than a testable theory.

articles.title: Unihemispheric Sleep in Dolphins and Birds
articles.gist: Describes animals that sleep with half the brain at a time and what the phenomenon reveals about the local control of sleep need.

articles.title: Reward Prediction Errors Meet Sensory Prediction Errors: One Signal or Two?
articles.gist: Compares dopaminergic reward errors with cortical sensory prediction errors and asks whether a shared computational motif could explain both under a single learning framework.

articles.title: Zen Koans as Training in Non-Conceptual Attention
articles.gist: Explores how koan practice is used to break habitual thinking, drawing on classical commentary and modern accounts of what the practice feels like.

articles.title: Surprise Signals in Mouse Visual Cortex After Visuomotor Mismatch
articles.gist: Two-photon imaging shows layer 2/3 neurons respond strongly when visual flow fails to match running speed, interpreted as evidence for mismatch error neurons learned through experience.

articles.title: Engram Cells and the Search for the Physical Memory Trace
articles.gist: Reviews tagging and reactivation experiments that label cells active during learning, asking whether silenced or artificially activated engrams are the memory or merely its access key.

articles.title: Working Memory Without Persistent Activity: Activity-Silent Traces
articles.gist: Proposes that short-term synaptic dynamics can hold information between bursts of spikes, and reviews decoding studies that find reactivation by non-specific pulses.

articles.title: Orexin Neurons and the Switch Between Wake and Sleep
articles.gist: Explains how hypothalamic orexin cells stabilise wakefulness, how their loss causes narcolepsy, and how flip-flop models of state transitions have been revised.

articles.title: Place Cells Remap Without Moving: Contextual Drift Across Weeks
articles.gist: Chronic calcium imaging in CA1 shows place fields shift gradually over days even in an unchanged environment, raising questions about what a stable spatial memory actually is.

articles.title: Reward Prediction Errors in the Human Midbrain: High-Field fMRI Evidence
articles.gist: Reports signals consistent with prediction errors in the human ventral tegmental area using 7T imaging, with careful handling of physiological noise.

articles.title: Diffusion MRI Tractography and the Problem of False Positives
articles.gist: Evaluates how well tractography reconstructs known anatomy, using phantom and tracer comparisons, and cautions against reading white matter maps as wiring diagrams.

articles.title: Experience-Dependent Plasticity in the Visual Cortex: Critical Periods
articles.gist: Reviews ocular dominance plasticity, the role of inhibitory maturation in opening and closing critical periods, and reactivation in adulthood.

articles.title: Systems Consolidation Reconsidered: Do Memories Ever Leave the Hippocampus?
articles.gist: Weighs standard consolidation against multiple-trace and transformation accounts using lesion timing, imaging of remote recall and the persistence of detail.

articles.title: Retinotopic Mapping at Ultra-High Field: Laminar Responses
articles.gist: Uses 7T fMRI to resolve depth-dependent responses in human V1, discussing draining-vein confounds and what laminar profiles can say about feedback.

articles.title: Precision-Weighting and Neuromodulators: Acetylcholine as a Gain Knob
articles.gist: Proposes that cholinergic tone sets the relative weight of bottom-up evidence against priors, and tests the idea with pharmacology and auditory oddball paradigms.

articles.title: Binocular Disparity and the Neural Basis of Stereo Depth
articles.gist: Records disparity-tuned neurons in V1 and V2 and tests which of them correlate with perceptual judgments in a depth discrimination task.

articles.title: Extra-Classical Receptive Fields as Evidence for Feedback Prediction
articles.gist: Argues that end-stopping and surround suppression in V1 reflect top-down predictions from higher areas, reviewing cooling and optogenetic feedback manipulations.

articles.title: Motor Preparation Without Movement: Null Space Dynamics
articles.gist: Shows that preparatory activity in premotor cortex lies in dimensions that do not drive muscles, explaining how plans can build up silently before an action.

articles.title: Sharpening Chisels and Plane Irons Without Obsession
articles.gist: A practical piece on getting a sharp edge with just a few stones and a strop, arguing that fussing over mirror polish wastes workshop time.

articles.title: Orientation Selectivity in V1: Feedforward or Recurrent?
articles.gist: Revisits the origin of orientation tuning, comparing the classic Hubel and Wiesel wiring with recurrent amplification models in light of intracellular recordings and silencing experiments.

articles.title: Replay and Reward: How Sharp-Wave Ripples Shape Value Learning
articles.gist: Shows that hippocampal replay preferentially visits rewarded locations and may train value estimates in striatum, linking offline memory reactivation to reinforcement learning.

articles.title: Dynamical Systems for Decision Making: From Drift Diffusion to Networks
articles.gist: Compares accumulation-to-bound models with attractor networks, asking what the neural recordings from parietal cortex can and cannot discriminate between.

articles.title: Hand-Cut Dovetails: Layout, Sawing and Paring
articles.gist: A step-by-step guide to cutting tight half-blind and through dovetail joints with hand tools, including marking gauges, sawing to the line and chisel work.

articles.title: Schema, Prior Knowledge and Fast Learning in Rodents
articles.gist: Rats learning new flavour-place pairs consolidate within a day if a schema exists, challenging the long timescale of classic systems consolidation.

articles.title: Serotonin and Patience: Reward Waiting in the Dorsal Raphe
articles.gist: Optogenetic stimulation of raphe neurons increases waiting for delayed rewards, and the paper considers whether serotonin encodes a time horizon or a punishment expectation.

articles.title: Attractor Dynamics in Head Direction Circuits
articles.gist: Shows that head direction cells form a ring attractor whose activity persists in the dark, using Drosophila and rodent recordings to test the predicted connectivity.

articles.title: Manifold Structure in Hippocampal Population Activity During Navigation
articles.gist: Uses dimensionality reduction on large-scale recordings to show that hippocampal activity traces a low-dimensional manifold that reorganises across environments.

articles.title: Feature-Based Attention Spreads Across the Visual Field
articles.gist: Reports that attending to a colour or direction in one location boosts matching neurons everywhere, supporting a global feature similarity gain model.

articles.title: Deep Convolutional Networks as Models of Ventral Stream Responses
articles.gist: Compares layers of trained networks with neural responses in V4 and inferotemporal cortex, and asks which findings survive when stimuli and training sets are changed.

articles.title: Building a Workbench From Construction Lumber
articles.gist: A weekend project: a sturdy Roubo-style bench built from construction-grade timber, with notes on flattening, joinery and the vises worth paying for.

articles.title: Offline RL for Neuroscientists: Learning From a Fixed Dataset
articles.gist: A blog post explaining why standard temporal difference learning fails without exploration, and whether animals might use analogous conservative strategies when replaying past experience.

articles.title: Prediction Errors in Population Geometry: A Low-Dimensional View
articles.gist: Examines whether prediction-error responses occupy a distinct subspace in population activity, so that downstream readouts can separate surprise from stimulus identity.

articles.title: Dopamine Neurons Encode a Distribution of Future Rewards
articles.gist: Shows that different dopamine neurons have different optimism levels, collectively representing the full reward distribution as in distributional reinforcement learning, tested in mice with variable reward sizes.

articles.title: Slow Oscillations and Spindles: The Coupling That Consolidates
articles.gist: Reports that nesting of sleep spindles within slow oscillation up-states predicts overnight memory retention, and discusses causal tests using acoustic stimulation.

articles.title: Sharp-Wave Ripples Are Necessary for Spatial Memory Consolidation
articles.gist: Closed-loop disruption of ripples after learning impairs later performance in rats, giving causal evidence that offline replay does real work.

articles.title: Targeted Memory Reactivation Through Odour and Sound Cues During Sleep
articles.gist: Participants who received learning-associated cues while asleep showed improved recall afterwards, supporting the idea that reactivation drives consolidation.

articles.title: Biased Competition and the Neural Basis of Selective Attention
articles.gist: Revisits the theory in which stimuli compete for neural representation and attention biases the outcome, using single-unit recordings from V2 and V4.

articles.title: Small Samples and Brain-Wide Association Studies
articles.gist: Demonstrates that reproducible associations between brain imaging and behaviour need thousands of participants, with consequences for how studies should be planned.

articles.title: Neuromodulation of Plasticity: Acetylcholine and Learning Windows
articles.gist: Describes how cholinergic tone opens windows for cortical plasticity and why this matters for perceptual learning and recovery after injury.

articles.title: Value Representations in Orbitofrontal Population Codes
articles.gist: Analyses high-dimensional orbitofrontal activity during economic choice and finds value is encoded in a stable low-dimensional axis alongside context-dependent dimensions.

articles.title: The Mind in Early Buddhism: What the Pali Discourses Actually Say
articles.gist: A close reading of early canonical texts on consciousness and mental factors, separating the original claims from later scholastic elaboration.

articles.title: Criticality in the Brain: Evidence and Controversy
articles.gist: Examines whether neuronal avalanches imply a critical state, and highlights statistical pitfalls in fitting power laws to recordings.

articles.title: Face Patches and the Origin of Category Selectivity
articles.gist: Reviews macaque face patch recordings and the debate about whether such regions arise from experience, innate wiring or both, citing face-deprived rearing studies.

articles.title: Mismatch Negativity Revisited: Adaptation, Prediction or Both?
articles.gist: Reconsiders the auditory mismatch response with roving-oddball designs that separate stimulus-specific adaptation from genuine violations of learned regularities.

articles.title: The Attentional Blink and the Limits of Temporal Selection
articles.gist: Reconsiders why a second target is missed within about half a second of the first, comparing resource depletion and selection-gating accounts.

articles.title: No-Self and the Neuroscience of Self-Models
articles.gist: An essay comparing the Buddhist doctrine of anatta with scientific accounts of the self as a constructed model, and where the analogy breaks down.

articles.title: Sleep Deprivation and Cognitive Performance: A Meta-Analysis
articles.gist: Aggregates studies of attention, working memory and decision-making after sleep loss, with notes on publication bias and the heterogeneity of tasks.

articles.title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning in Prefrontal Networks
articles.gist: Shows that recurrent networks trained on many tasks learn their own learning algorithm, and suggests prefrontal dynamics and dopamine together implement similar fast adaptation.

articles.title: Exploration Is Not Noise: Directed Uncertainty-Seeking in Humans
articles.gist: Behavioural modelling shows people add information bonuses to uncertain options rather than simply choosing at random, with frontopolar activity tracking relative uncertainty.

articles.title: Basal Ganglia Loops and the Initiation of Voluntary Movement
articles.gist: Reviews direct and indirect pathway models of movement selection and the observation that both pathways are active during initiation.

articles.title: The Basal Ganglia as a Selection Machine: Actor-Critic Mappings
articles.gist: Revisits the proposal that dorsal striatum implements the actor and ventral striatum the critic, weighing anatomical, lesion and recording evidence.

articles.title: Alpha Oscillations as a Gating Mechanism for Visual Attention
articles.gist: Reviews evidence that alpha power increases over cortex representing ignored locations, and asks whether this reflects active inhibition or passive idling.

articles.title: Why Do We Forget? Interference, Decay and Active Erasure
articles.gist: Contrasts theories of forgetting and argues that some forgetting is adaptive and regulated, citing dopamine-driven forgetting in flies and rodent work on engram accessibility.

articles.title: The Glymphatic System: Does the Sleeping Brain Take Out the Trash?
articles.gist: A critical look at claims that cerebrospinal fluid flow clears metabolites during sleep, disputing measurements and discussing the role of anaesthetics.

articles.title: Attention Deficits in ADHD: A Systems View
articles.gist: A review of dopaminergic and noradrenergic hypotheses, cortical development findings and attention network measures in people diagnosed with ADHD.

articles.title: Representational Geometry of Object Categories in IT Population Responses
articles.gist: Uses geometry methods to show that category manifolds become more linearly separable along the ventral stream, with comparisons to deep networks.

articles.title: Astrocytes and Synaptic Modulation: More Than Support Cells?
articles.gist: Reviews tripartite synapse claims, calcium signalling in astrocytes and the controversy over gliotransmission.

articles.title: Temporal Difference Learning Beyond the Single Trial
articles.gist: Extends the classic temporal difference account to long timescales, discussing eligibility traces, credit assignment across delays and how dopamine ramps might reflect value gradients.

articles.title: Mortise and Tenon Strength: What the Tests Show
articles.gist: Summarises destructive tests of traditional joints against screws and dowels, discussing glue surface, draw-boring and the real limits of furniture joinery.

articles.title: Cortical Dynamics During Speech Production
articles.gist: Analyses ECoG and Neuropixels recordings from human speech cortex to show that articulation is generated through structured rotational dynamics.

articles.title: Understanding Wood Movement Before You Build a Table
articles.gist: Explains seasonal expansion across the grain, how to orient boards and attach tabletops with figure-8 fasteners, and what happens when you ignore these rules.

articles.title: Latent Variable Models of Spiking Data: Gaussian Process Factor Analysis
articles.gist: A methods tutorial on extracting smooth trajectories from simultaneously recorded neurons, with practical advice on regularisation and model selection.

articles.title: Theta Sequences and the Planning of Routes
articles.gist: Shows that compressed sweeps of place-cell activity within each theta cycle look ahead of the animal at choice points, with implications for deliberation.

articles.title: Connectivity Constraints on Network Dynamics: Learning in Spiking Models
articles.gist: Shows how local plasticity rules sculpt the recurrent connectivity that supports stable sequences and what that implies for the structure of trained networks.
